subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & product fit (SDK, streaming, function-calling)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme.com>, Tom Landry <tom.landry@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & product fit (SDK, streaming, function-calling)

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the integration topics we covered so we’re aligned on next steps. Please reply if I missed anything.

Key pain / goals (your team)
- High throughput customer support reranking: reduce average handle time for CS agents by surfacing the top 3 responses from a retrieval+reranker flow.
- Deterministic structured outputs for tickets (priority, category, recommended SLA, suggested tags) to populate your ticketing system.
- Low-latency streaming for agent-facing suggestions (sub-200ms token latency target for short prompts).
- Tight security controls + ability to run in a VPC/private deployment for PII-sensitive data.

Product fit summary (how Redwood can help)
- Embeddings + reranking: we recommend an embeddings index + a lightweight reranker in Redwood to return ranked passages; embeddings are incremental so we can sample performance quickly.
- Structured outputs & function-calling: use Redwood’s function-calling to return JSON-schema validated outputs (priority/category/tags). We can also stream tokens while validating final JSON structure server-side to meet UI UX needs.
- Streaming & latency: our runtime supports streaming responses with partial results and prefix caching; we’ll recommend a batching window that keeps tail latency under your 200ms SLO for short prompts.
- SDK changes: minimal — we provide a small client patch (see attached redwood_sdk_patch.diff) to support the function-calling helper and structured-output parsing.

Open questions we flagged
- Can you confirm the expected QPS during peak hours? We need this to size a dedicated pool for the POC.
- Which ticket fields must be strictly schema-validated vs. optional?
- Any redlines in procurement/security we should expect (e.g., IP clauses, data residency)?

Next steps
- I’ll send a short integration proposal + timeline (attached).
- Dev: we’ll provide an SDK patch + sample function schema by EOD Wed (Dev & Rishi).
- Your side: confirm QPS estimate and list of required ticket fields by EOD Thu.
- Schedule follow-up technical sync: can we target Thu 10:00 AM PT?

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, integration_diagram.png, redwood_sdk_patch.diff

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Landry <tom.landry@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & product fit (SDK, streaming, function-calling)

Thanks Marissa — really clear summary, appreciate it. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Peak QPS: our CS peak is around 120 reqs/minute for the reranker layer (we expect bursts to 200).
- Ticket fields: required = priority (P0/P1/P2), category (billing/tech/account), customer_tier, recommended_sla. Optional = suggested_tags, recommended_owner.
- Security: SOC2 + customer-managed KMS are must-haves. We’ll share our security questionnaire but we’re generally okay exploring Redwood Private if needed.

We can do Thu 10:00 AM PT for the technical sync — Tom and I will join. Looking forward to the SDK patch.

Best,
Alicia
Head of Customer Experience, Acme Corp
Alicia.Gomez@acme.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.example>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@acme.com>, Tom Landry <tom.landry@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & product fit (SDK, streaming, function-calling)

Hi Alicia / Tom —

Thanks for the QPS and field list — that’s super helpful. Quick engineering notes ahead of Thu’s call: 

1) Sizing: 120 QPS steady (200 burst) looks like a small Dedicated pool with autoscale headroom; I’ll put together a capacity estimate for the POC.

2) SDK patch + sample flow: attached patch contains a small helper for function-calling that: 
   - wraps the JSON-schema validator on the server side,
   - exposes a streaming iterator for partial suggestions, and
   - includes a reranker example using embeddings + a lightweight cross-encoder.

3) Structured outputs: we’ll provide a sample function schema for the required fields you listed. In the SDK example we’ll: 
   - stream incremental suggestions to the frontend,
   - buffer until valid JSON is produced or until a final token triggers validation, and
   - emit a validated JSON payload to be consumed by your ticketing ingestion service.

4) Security & Private deployment: we support customer-managed KMS and can scope the POC in Redwood Private (VPC peering) if you need L3 isolation for PII. I’ll loop in our security team after the call.

Deliverables before Thu 10:00 AM PT
- SDK patch + README (attached) — ETA: EOD Wed
- Capacity estimate for POC — ETA: EOD Wed
- Sample JSON-schema functions for required ticket fields — ETA: EOD Wed

If anything changes on your side, ping me here.
— Dev
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.example
